gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: It's an open public seafront, so pushchairs come along with no fuss. I would stick to the promenade and the Greensward, as the sand is hard going.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Dogs are welcome on a lead, but not on the beach, apart from guide dogs. With the jet noise and the crowds, I would think hard about whether yours would be happier at home.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: You can bring your own picnic, and the council asks you to use the bins and cut down on single use plastic. Nothing is said about alcohol for the show, and Clacton town centre has a street drinking order, so I would leave it at home to be safe.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: I haven't seen a rule either way. Chairs and windbreaks are what I see most people bring, and I would ask the show before packing a gazebo, as it blocks the view for everyone behind you.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: When I last checked there were no refill points listed for the show. I would bring more water than you think you need, as there's very little shade on the front.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There's a Changing Places toilet next to the West Greensward toilets, with a hoist and changing bench. It needs an entrance key from the council, and a Radar key won't open it, so I would apply well before the show.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: The whole show is free to watch, so there are no tickets for anyone. In 2026 there was a courtesy shuttle for Blue Badge holders and one carer from the West Road car park.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I haven't found anything about hearing loops or BSL for the show. I would email the airshow team before you go, and Radio Airshow on Actual Radio carried the commentary in 2026 if that helps.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There's no calm or sensory space listed. The high ground at Holland on Sea is a quieter place to watch, further from the crowds, and that may work for you.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: It's a public seafront with no gates, so you can pop into town and come back. Police searches and vehicle checks were part of the security in 2026, so I would keep your bags light.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: In 2026 there were first aid points at the Hastings Avenue seafront car park, at Pier Gap and in the middle of the event site. I would pick up a free coloured wristband for each child from a Beach Patrol office or a steward, as it makes reuniting lost children much quicker.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it's fresh, dress in layers to keep warm, and the cafés and the pier are close by if a shower rolls in.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

Clacton runs on a Thursday and a Friday, and the two days feel quite different. The Thursday goes on into the evening, while the Friday is a straight daytime show. I would think about how late your group can realistically stay, as that usually decides it.

Dates26 and 27 August 2027
OpeningFrom 11:00 (2026)
TwilightThursday in 2026
EntryFree both days
ThursdayIn 2026 the site was open 11:00 to 22:00. Afternoon flying with the Red Arrows, then a twilight display with the Desert Spitfire, the Firebirds, the MiG-17 and Otto the Helicopter’s pyrotechnics, and fireworks at Clacton Pier after.
FridayIn 2026 the site was open 11:00 to 17:00. A full afternoon of flying with the Red Arrows again, and the P-51D Mustang “Moonbeam McSwine” was a Friday only act. You’re heading home in daylight.

Who’s coming?

What are you after?

How late can you stay?

I Would Pick The Thursday

  1. WhyYou get the afternoon flying and then the twilight display, with lit up aircraft and pyrotechnics over the sea. Children love to see it, and in 2026 there were fireworks at the pier to finish.
  2. Good to knowThe twilight display ran in 2026, but when I last checked it hadn’t been confirmed for 2027. I would check before you plan the whole day round it.
  3. Getting thereIn 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 22:00. If you’re on the train, I would look up the last one home before you set off.

I Would Pick The Friday

  1. WhyIt’s a full afternoon of flying with the Red Arrows, and you’re done by teatime. That might work for your family if little ones flag by late afternoon.
  2. Good to knowIn 2025 the Friday flying started at about 13:00, a little earlier than the Thursday. The 2027 times will be in the programme.
  3. Getting thereIn 2026 the last Park and Ride bus left the seafront at 18:30, so I wouldn’t hang about too long after the last display.
Jack’s tipIf you can do both, I would go on the Friday for the daytime flying and save the Thursday for a late afternoon arrival, a tea in town and the twilight display. Bring a warm top. It gets cool on the front once the sun goes.

Based on the 2026 show. The 2027 line-up and times may change.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

The flying is in the afternoon, so the ground show is what fills your morning. It all sits in the Airshow Village on the West Greensward, which opened at 11:00 on both days in 2026. There’s very little static aircraft display at Clacton, so think of it more as a seaside festival with an aviation theme.

WhereWest Greensward
Opens11:00 (2026)
CostFree to walk round
CashNo machines on site
In 2026

Replica Typhoon Cockpit

The RAF Careers Engagement team brought a replica Typhoon cockpit to sit in, along with RAF careers displays. I’ve said more about them in the .

In 2026

Batak Reaction Challenge

A wall of lights you have to hit as fast as you can. Children love to have a go, and it’s harder than it looks.

In 2026

STEM Activities

Hands on science and engineering stands aimed at getting young people thinking about careers in aviation. Worth a look if you have a curious one.

Bring cash

Trade Stands And Exhibitors

In 2026 there were stalls selling everything from natural pet food to handmade garden furniture and handcrafted goods from Indonesia. There are no cash machines on site, so I would bring some with you.

Pay as you go

Food Concessions

Local traders like Whippy Bro’s, Spud Box and Vintage Shakes were serving in 2026, and Combat 2 Coffee was back in the services area. For toilets and sit down meals, take a look at .

£6 (2026)

The Official Programme

The Ground Crew walk the site selling it, and it has the flying times in. I would buy one early so you can plan the afternoon.

Pay as you go

Clacton Pier

Just east of the show, with rides, arcades and food. It’s a handy break if the village gets too busy, and the nearest cash machine is there too.

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the seafront first and set up your chairs or blanket. The Greensward fills quickly.
  2. Then take a look roundOnce you’re set, walk the village. Visit the RAF stand, speak to any crews you spot, check out the trade stalls and see what food is on.
  3. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the first aircraft appears, as the queues build fast once it starts.
  4. Use the gapsIf you aren’t waiting for a particular display, use it as a toilet or food break. The stalls are much quieter while everyone is looking up.
Jack’s tipI would head to the RAF stand soon after saving your pitch. It’s quieter before the bulk of the crowds arrive, so children have a better chance of a go in the cockpit without a long wait.

Exhibitors and attractions change each year, so the 2027 village may look different.

support.html:
Keep The Show Free

Clacton is free to watch, but it costs a lot to put on. The council asks visitors to chip in where they can, and I think it’s worth doing if you’ve had a good day. Even a few pounds in a bucket helps keep it going.

EntryFree
Programme£6 (2026)
DonateOnline or in the buckets
£6 (2026)

Buy The Programme

The money goes straight back into the show. In 2026 you could buy one from the Ground Crew on site, the Visitor Information Centre, Clacton station, the Beach Patrol office or Clacton Pier.

Any amount

Bucket Collections

There are bucket collections around the show. I would keep some change in your pocket, as there are no cash machines on the site.

Any amount

Donate Online

If you don’t carry cash, you can give through the official website before or after the show. This may work for you if you’re watching from home on the radio too.

For businesses

Sponsors And Programme Adverts

Local firms can sponsor a display or take an advert in the programme. In 2026 adverts started at £250 plus VAT for a quarter page.

Make a donationGive any amount online to the showSponsors and partnersSponsorship, hospitality and programme adverts
Jack’s tipI buy the programme first thing. It tells you roughly when each display is on, so you know when to save your spot and when to nip off for food, and it’s helping the show at the same time.

Programme prices and ways to give may change for 2027.

skipped.flights: The show doesn't offer any pleasure, helicopter or warbird flights. Clacton Aero Club sells trial lessons in a Cessna from its own grass airfield on West Road, but that's a flying school away from the show site and not linked to the airshow, so I left it out.

notes: 1) The twilight display was confirmed for Thursday 27 August 2026 but not yet for 2027; the page already says this, so it's correct. 2) Help On Show Days, Lost Each Other: the official FAQ has a free colour coded wristband scheme for children (from the TDC Beach Patrol offices and stewards) and lost persons points at the Beach Patrol offices; the page doesn't mention these, so it may be worth a line there (https://clactonairshow.com/faqs/). 3) Feeling Unwell only mentions stewards and lifeguards; in 2026 there were three first aid points (Hastings Avenue seafront car park, Pier Gap and the centre of the event site). 4) The official FAQ lists the high ground at Holland on Sea as a quieter viewing spot, which isn't in Where to watch. 5) West Road car park was £10 a car in 2026 (£20 for vans and motorhomes), run by the Rotary Club; the page doesn't give the price. 6) In 2026 fireworks followed the twilight flights at Clacton Pier; the page mentions pyrotechnics but not the fireworks. 7) The Food and facilities 'Supporting the show' paragraph could now just point to the new Keep the show free tab. 8) I avoided the 'opened up aircraft and merch' line in the ground show, because Clacton has very little static display advertised.
